**Finding: compliant (no redline proposed).**

The Agreement contains no audit, inspection or verification right exercisable against Sparkling. I checked every plausible location:

- **§ 3 Restrictions on Use (p0030–p0039)** — imposes copying, reverse-engineering, sublicence and service-bureau restrictions, but attaches no compliance-verification or inspection mechanic.
- **§ 10 / Page 5 (Maintenance and Support)** — telephone support, update and repair services only; no right of access to our systems.
- **§ 14 Confidentiality (p0095)** — only defines Confidential Information to include "accounting records for which access is obtained by the other party pursuant to this Agreement"; it presupposes access granted elsewhere and creates none.
- **§ 20 / Page 10 (General Matters)** — notices, waiver, assignment, independent contractor, force majeure, severability, governing law; no records or inspection provision.
- Full-text searches for audit, inspection, records, examine, monitor, remote access and premises returned nothing further.

Because Garman has no audit right at all, our exposure sits above the preferred position (no frequency, notice, cost-allocation or system-access parameters are needed), so the AUDIT rule requires no change. Inserting the preferred frequency/notice/cost limits would only manufacture a Vendor audit right that does not exist today.
